title: The cow
hookLine: told to sacrifice a cow, the people ask question after question and make it harder (2:67–71)

lines: WHICH BRAND? WHOLE OR TWO PERCENT?
ONE CARTON THAT MAY NOT EXIST.
cards: Someone asks you to pick up milk on the way home. Easy. But you text back: which brand?
Whole or two percent? Gallon or half? By the fourth message, you're standing in the aisle hunting for one carton that may not exist, annoyed at the person who just wanted milk.
The longest surah in the Qur'an is named after a story like that. Today: the cow.

teach.b: Musa tells his people, in Pickthall's words: “Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye sacrifice a cow.” Any cow would have done. But they answer: are you making fun of us?
God forbid, Musa says, that I should be one of the foolish. So they ask: what is she? Not old, not young, in between.

teach.h: WHAT AGE? WHAT COLOR? WHICH ONE?
teach.b: What color? Yellow, bright, a pleasure to look at. They ask again: all cows look alike to us.
A cow never yoked to plow the earth or water the fields, whole, without a mark on her. By now, finding her is hard.
So they sacrificed her, the verse says, though they almost didn't. The verses that follow give the reason: a man had been killed, and the people were blaming one another.

The commentators fill in the rest: the cow was the way the killer would be revealed. Ibn Abbas, in a report in at-Tabari's commentary, puts the lesson plainly: if they had sacrificed any cow, it would have been enough.
They made it hard on themselves, and so it was made hard for them.

A hadith in Bukhari says the religion is ease, and nobody makes it too hard without it overpowering them. Another warns against asking about something that wasn't forbidden until the question made it so.
The question isn't the problem; al-Baqarah is full of honest questions. The problem is the question that's really a delay.

how: Muslim teachers often cite the story of the cow, and the hadith that the religion is ease, when warning against piling up needless questions or making religious practice harder than it was given.

games.q: Musa tells you: God commands you to sacrifice a cow. what do you do?
o: ask what age she should be.
games.why: in the story they asked whether he was joking, then asked age, color and kind, until finding her was hard. Ibn Abbas: any cow would have been enough.

practice: Think of one thing you keep complicating: the email that needs perfect wording, the call waiting for the right moment, the prayer you'll start once your life is in order.
Name it, and picture its plainest version, with no more questions, while you breathe.

wordCard.voice: The cow. Al-Baqarah's namesake: a simple command made hard by question after question, until the people almost didn't do it. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a cow; the name of the Qur'an's second and longest surah.

carryVoice: Your line: don't make it harder. Any cow at all would have done. Until tomorrow.
